subtitle: Meet it · discover it · imagine with it

sections.title: Meet the bicycle
sections.visualLabel: A large side-view bicycle ready to explore
sections.storyLead: A bicycle is waiting. Before we ride, let us look closely and listen for one small sound.
sections.lookPrompt: Find both wheels. Then look for the bell near the handle.

beats.label: READY TO ROLL
beats.text: A bicycle is a wheeled vehicle. The rider supplies the power that helps it move.

beats.label: RING, RING
beats.text: A bicycle may have a bell. Its ringing sound can help signal that a rider is nearby.

sections.remember: A rider powers the bicycle, and a bell can make a useful signal.
sections.childPrompt: Point to the two wheels. Now tap the bell.

sections.title: Seven parts to find
sections.visualLabel: A large bicycle with seven tappable part labels
sections.storyLead: The whole bicycle stays large on the screen. Tap a label and the matching part wakes up.
sections.lookPrompt: Find: seat, pedal, wheel, bell, handle, carrier, brake.

beats.label: THE SEVEN WORDS
beats.text: Learn the bicycle as one whole object first. Then locate these seven visible parts.

beats.label: GO · TURN · SLOW
beats.text: Your foot pushes the pedal. The wheel rolls, the handle steers, and the brake helps the bicycle slow down.

beats.label: SEAT · BELL · CARRIER
beats.text: Find the seat, bell and carrier. A bell and a carrier are useful parts that some bicycles have and some do not.

sections.remember: First see the whole bicycle. Then learn where each named part belongs.
sections.childPrompt: Tap all seven labels. Choose one part and say its name.

sections.title: How does the pedal make it go?
sections.visualLabel: A slow inspectable pedal, crank, chain and back-wheel demonstration
sections.storyLead: This is an extra look inside the machine. These inner-part words explain what happens; they are not a word list you have to memorise.
sections.lookPrompt: Press Play. Watch one thing begin moving, then the next.

beats.label: WATCH THE MOTION TRAVEL
beats.text: The movement travels through connected parts. Pause the demonstration anywhere and follow the path.

beats.label: WHAT THE RIDER FEELS
beats.text: From the outside it feels simple: your foot pushes a pedal, and pedalling helps the bicycle move.

sections.remember: The inner motion is an explanation to watch and understand, not a list to memorise.
sections.childPrompt: Replay it slowly. Can you point to the part that moves after the pedal?

sections.title: Ring, listen, say
sections.visualLabel: A bicycle bell beside playful word cards
sections.storyLead: The bicycle gives us a sound to notice and words to play with.
sections.lookPrompt: Tap the bell, then say the word cards slowly.

beats.label: BELL SOUND
beats.text: A bicycle bell makes a ringing sound. Ringing can also tell others that a rider is nearby.

beats.label: SHORT A
beats.text: Cat, cap and map share the same short-a sound in the middle.

beats.label: A OR AN?
beats.text: Listen to the first sound when you choose a or an.

sections.remember: Listen closely: sounds can help you notice patterns in words.
sections.childPrompt: Ring the bell. Then say: cat, cap, map; a bicycle; an apple.

sections.title: Where could it take you?
sections.visualLabel: An original playful bicycle in an imaginative sky
sections.storyLead: Now the bicycle can leave the workshop. There is no one correct destination.
sections.lookPrompt: Choose a place, or invent your own place in your head.

beats.label: CHOOSE A DESTINATION
beats.text: Imagine a bicycle that can take you somewhere surprising. Your idea can be completely different from anyone else's.

beats.label: WHAT HAPPENS THERE?
beats.text: Give your ride one tiny story: where do you arrive, what do you notice, and what happens next?

sections.remember: An imaginative answer belongs to the child; it is not marked right or wrong.
sections.childPrompt: Tell your magic ride in three tiny steps, or just imagine it quietly.

sections.title: Follow a tiny ride story
sections.visualLabel: Three original story cards showing a simple ride sequence
sections.storyLead: A tiny story gives us clues. We can find a detail, put actions in order, and explain a simple reason.
sections.lookPrompt: Read the three actions. Which happens first?

beats.label: TINY STORY
beats.text: Ria fastens her helmet. She checks the brakes. Then she begins to pedal.

beats.label: FIND THE CLUES
beats.text: Action words and order words help us understand what happened and why.

sections.remember: Find the actions first. Then use the clues to understand the story.
sections.childPrompt: Retell the tiny story: first, next, last.

sections.title: Get ready before you go
sections.visualLabel: A bicycle, helmet and simple pre-ride check
sections.storyLead: The ride is almost ready. A few simple checks come before moving off.
sections.lookPrompt: Find the helmet, brakes and tyres.

beats.label: HELMET
beats.text: Fasten a properly fitted cycling helmet before you ride. It helps protect the head.

beats.label: BRAKES · TYRES
beats.text: Check that the brakes work and the tyres are ready. A bell can help signal when one is fitted.

sections.childPrompt: Tap the three checks in order: helmet, brakes, tyres.
